mechanism.CORRECTED_2026_08_07: scientific-reviewer agent ab2d3748d0b00c78c corrected the mechanism from fn_phase to ResetNearestExtrap int-dtype truncation. mechanism.root: PPTitan template ships Planet.PfreezeUpper_MPa = 230 as a Python int; the whole cache was built with that int passed through to GetPfreeze (HydroEOS.py:1239) as PUpper_MPa. The melt-EOS grid np.arange(PfreezeLower, PfreezeUpper, PfreezeRes) has Pmax=229.96 < PfreezeUpper=230, so the search upper endpoint P=230 ALWAYS exceeds Pmax and is clamped by ResetNearestExtrap.
mechanism.smoking_gun: ResetNearestExtrap (DataManip.py:15-35) size-1 branch: line 26 outVar1=np.array(var1) PRESERVES the input int64 dtype (lines 23-24's float-promotion via +0.0 is overwritten for size-1); line 31 then assigns float max1=229.96 into that int array -> TRUNCATES to 229. VERIFIED: ResetNearestExtrap(230,...) -> clamps to 229.0; ResetNearestExtrap(230.0,...) -> 229.96. Generalizes to T: ResetNearestExtrap(...,280,...) -> 274.0 vs 274.9. Phase at P=229 is liquid(0); phase at correct clamp 229.96 is ice III(3).
mechanism.consequence: GetPfreeze line 1262 sign-test phaseChange(PLower)*phaseChange(PUpper): int-truncated PUpper=229 evaluates liquid -> product<0 -> routes to GetZero bracketing on a discontinuous step function -> fails -> NoIceLiquidTransitionError -> node mislabeled frozen/None. float PUpper clamps to 229.96 -> ice III -> product>0 -> brute-force arange scan -> correctly finds the ice-Ih->liquid transition ~200 MPa -> ocean.
mechanism.co_causal_note: reviewer verified raising PfreezeUpper to an INT 250/300 ALSO repairs the node (grid then extends past 230, endpoint no longer clamps). So the defect is the joint condition (int PUpper) AND (PUpper >= melt-EOS Pmax so endpoint clamps) AND (Pmax fractional part flips phase on truncation). Float coercion fixes it; so does extending the grid. The deeper fix is dtype=float in ResetNearestExtrap.
mechanism.nacl_framing: reviewer note: an ISOLATED GetPfreeze NaCl call builds ocean for both int/float (229 and 229.96 both liquid at Tb=252 for NaCl); the failure reproduces only through the FULL build_single_structure melt-EOS reconstruction path. The per-node onset-column table (below) is the trustworthy evidence; do NOT expect a standalone fn_phase(230) flip for NaCl.
mechanism.physical_correctness: float path is correct: at 230 MPa / 252 K, dilute-salinity Titan is in the HP-ice (ice III) regime BELOW a real ocean whose Ih->liquid top sits ~193-208 MPa (matches both cache neighbors). Near the ice Ih-III-liquid triple point (~209 MPa), just under the 230 MPa search ceiling -- why the artifact localizes to a single Tb node one step into the ocean region.
